claims.text: The initial equiatomic NbMoTaW alloy is an as-cast, homogenized, single-phase BCC material.
Adding 0.5 at.% Y and thermomechanical processing will produce a fine, uniform dispersion of approximately 20–50 nm Y2O3 nanoparticles.
The Y2O3 nanoparticles will be dispersed within the BCC matrix and along grain boundaries.
Y2O3 particles act as sinks for irradiation defects and helium.
Defect and helium trapping by Y2O3 particles reduces helium-bubble nucleation and growth.
Grain-boundary pinning by Y2O3 inhibits crack propagation and increases room-temperature ductility.
The Y2O3 particle volume fraction will be below 1%.
A Y2O3 volume fraction below 1% will minimally perturb the BCC lattice and preserve high-temperature strength.
Untreated NbMoTaW has approximately 5% room-temperature tensile elongation.
Untreated NbMoTaW has a yield strength of approximately 600 MPa at 1600 °C.
Untreated NbMoTaW exhibits approximately 2 vol.% swelling under the specified irradiation condition.
The intervention will increase room-temperature tensile elongation from approximately 5% to at least 12%.
The intervention will keep the 1600 °C yield-strength change within 10% of untreated NbMoTaW.
The intervention will reduce volumetric void swelling by at least 50% after 1 dpa irradiation with 2 MeV helium at 400 °C.
The intervention preserves BCC structural stability.
The irradiation-tolerance effect applies at helium implantation energies of 0.5–2 MeV, doses up to 1 dpa, and irradiation temperatures of 25–800 °C.
The estimated ductility and swelling improvements are based on analogous oxide-dispersion-strengthened tungsten systems.

contradictions.description: The predicted room-temperature elongation is at least 12%, but falsification requires elongation below 10%; results from 10% to below 12% would miss the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
The predicted swelling reduction is at least 50%, but falsification requires less than 30%; reductions from 30% to below 50% would miss the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
The intervention specifies adding elemental Y during melting but provides no oxygen source or oxidation step capable of establishing the claimed Y2O3 nanoparticle dispersion.
